answers.headline: No. Physically harming someone is a crime in Germany, with up to 5 years in prison.
answers.summary: Assault (Körperverletzung) covers physically mistreating someone or damaging their health. Even an attempt is punishable. Self-defence (Notwehr) can be lawful.
answers.penalties: Up to 5 years in prison or a fine; more for dangerous or serious assault.

answers.headline: No. Offering a police officer or other official a benefit to break their duties is a crime.
answers.summary: Offering, promising or giving a public official, including a police officer, an advantage in return for an act that breaks their duties is bribery (Bestechung).
answers.penalties: 3 months to 5 years in prison; less in minor cases.

answers.headline: No. Buying something you know is stolen is a crime (handling stolen goods).
answers.summary: Buying or otherwise acquiring goods that someone else stole, to benefit yourself or another person, is handling stolen goods (Hehlerei). Unlike in some countries, German criminal law requires that you knew or accepted that the goods were stolen. Being merely careless isn’t a crime, but you may still have to give the goods back.
answers.penalties: Up to 5 years in prison or a fine.

answers.headline: No. The limit is 0.5‰ for drivers, and zero for new drivers and anyone under 21.
answers.summary: Driving a motor vehicle with 0.5‰ or more alcohol in the blood (0.25 mg/l in breath) is an offence. During the probation period and before age 21, drivers may not drink any alcohol before or while driving. Anyone, including cyclists, who drives any vehicle while unable to do so safely because of alcohol or drugs commits a crime, even below these limits.
conditions: Limit: 0.5‰ in blood (0.25 mg/l in breath) for motor vehicles
New drivers in probation and under-21s: no alcohol at all
Cannabis: 3.5 ng/ml THC in blood serum
answers.penalties: Over the limit: a fine and possible driving ban. Unable to drive safely: up to 1 year in prison or a fine, even on a bicycle.

answers.headline: No. Murder is punished with life imprisonment in Germany.
answers.summary: Killing someone counts as murder (Mord) when it’s done with particular motives or methods, such as greed, cruelty, treachery or to cover up another crime. Other intentional killing is manslaughter (Totschlag). Self-defence can be lawful in narrow circumstances.
answers.penalties: Murder: life imprisonment. Manslaughter: at least 5 years, life in especially serious cases.

answers.headline: Yes. Germans must own a valid ID card, but don’t have to carry it with them.
answers.summary: Germans aged 16 and over must have a valid ID card or passport and show it to authorities when asked, but the law doesn’t require carrying it at all times. If you can’t show it, police may take further steps to establish who you are.
conditions: You must own a valid ID from age 16
answers.penalties: Not owning a valid ID at all can be fined.

answers.headline: Yes, for adults: up to 25 g in public and up to 50 g and 3 plants at home.
answers.summary: Since April 2024, adults may possess cannabis for their own use within these limits and grow up to three plants at home. Smoking it is banned near children, within sight of schools, playgrounds, youth facilities and sports grounds (within 100 m of the entrance), and in pedestrian zones between 07:00 and 20:00. Selling and passing it on stay illegal.
conditions: Age 18 or over
Up to 25 g in public; up to 50 g at home
Up to 3 plants at home
No use near minors, schools or playgrounds; not in pedestrian zones 07:00–20:00
answers.penalties: Possessing more than the limits is an offence or a crime depending on the amount.

answers.headline: No. In Germany, secretly recording someone’s private words is a crime, even in your own call.
answers.summary: Recording the non-public spoken words of another person without their permission is a crime, and so is using or sharing such a recording. This applies even if you take part in the conversation yourself. Ask for consent before recording.
conditions: Allowed with the other person’s consent
answers.penalties: Up to 3 years in prison or a fine.
answers.activity: Recording a phone call without telling the other person

answers.headline: Only at New Year: adults may set off ordinary fireworks on 31 December and 1 January.
answers.summary: Category F2 fireworks (ordinary New Year rockets and bangers) may only be sold to consumers from 29 to 31 December and set off by adults on 31 December and 1 January. Setting off fireworks right next to churches, hospitals, children’s homes and care homes is always banned.
conditions: Age 18 or over
Only on 31 December and 1 January
Not near churches, hospitals, children’s or care homes
answers.penalties: Setting off fireworks outside these rules can be fined.
answers.regional_variation: Local authorities can ban fireworks near fire-sensitive buildings, and ban bangers in densely populated areas, even on 31 December and 1 January.

answers.headline: Swearing itself isn’t illegal, but insulting someone is a crime in Germany.
answers.summary: Using bad language in general isn’t punished. Insulting a person (Beleidigung), for example calling someone names or giving the middle finger, is a crime, and it’s punished more heavily if done in public or online.
answers.penalties: Up to 1 year in prison or a fine; up to 2 years if done in public, online or with physical contact.

answers.headline: No. Theft is a crime in Germany, with up to 5 years in prison.
answers.summary: Taking someone else’s movable property, intending to keep it unlawfully, is theft (Diebstahl). Even an attempt is punishable.
answers.penalties: Up to 5 years in prison or a fine.

answers.headline: Yes, as long as you don’t pick it up or hold it, and only use voice control or a quick glance.
answers.summary: Drivers may only use a phone or other electronic device if they don’t pick it up or hold it, and either use voice control and read-out functions or only glance at it briefly in a way suited to the traffic conditions.
conditions: Don’t pick up or hold the device
Voice control, or only a brief glance
answers.penalties: Using a hand-held phone while driving is fined, with penalty points.
answers.activity: Using a phone hands-free while driving

answers.headline: No. Injuring someone is a crime in Spain, and even hitting someone without injuring them is punished with a fine.
answers.summary: Causing an injury that needs medical treatment is the crime of lesiones. Minor injuries and hitting someone without causing injury are punished with fines, but only if the victim files a complaint.
answers.penalties: Injury needing treatment: 3 months to 3 years in prison or a fine. Minor injury: a fine of 1–3 months. Hitting without injury: a fine of 1–2 months.

answers.headline: No. Offering an official, including a police officer, a gift or payment is a crime in Spain.
answers.summary: Offering or giving any kind of gift or payment to an authority or public official, so they act against their duties, do or delay their job, or simply because of their position, is bribery (cohecho). The person paying gets the same prison and fine as the official.
answers.penalties: The same prison term and fine as the bribed official.

answers.headline: No. Buying goods you know were stolen is a crime in Spain.
answers.summary: Receiving, buying or hiding goods for gain, knowing they come from a crime against property, is handling stolen goods (receptación). The penalty is higher for items of cultural value, essential goods, or infrastructure such as cables.
answers.penalties: 6 months to 2 years in prison; 1 to 3 years in aggravated cases.

answers.headline: No. It’s banned to drive wearing headphones, earphones or an audio headset.
answers.summary: Driving with any audio headset, earphones or similar device connected to a sound player or receiver is banned. The only exception is certified intercom or navigation systems built into motorcycle and moped helmets.
answers.penalties: A traffic fine and points off your licence.

It’s 0.3 g/l (0.15 mg/l in breath) for the first two years after getting your licence, and for drivers of trucks, buses, taxis, school transport and emergency vehicles. Above 1.2 g/l (0.60 mg/l in breath), or when under the influence, it’s a crime.
conditions: General limit: 0.5 g/l blood (0.25 mg/l breath), cyclists included
New drivers (first 2 years) and professional drivers: 0.3 g/l (0.15 mg/l breath)
answers.penalties: Over the limit: an administrative fine and points. Over 1.2 g/l or under the influence: 3–6 months in prison, a fine or community service, plus losing your licence for 1–4 years.

answers.headline: No. Killing someone is punished with 10 to 25 years in prison in Spain, and up to life in the worst cases.
answers.summary: Killing someone is homicide (homicidio). It becomes murder (asesinato) with treachery, for payment, with cruelty, or to commit or hide another crime. Some murders, for example of a child under 16 or a vulnerable person, carry reviewable life imprisonment. Self-defence can be lawful in narrow circumstances.
answers.penalties: Homicide: 10–15 years. Murder: 15–25 years. Aggravated murder: reviewable life imprisonment.

answers.headline: No. Stealing is a crime in Spain: prison for items worth over €400, a fine below that.
answers.summary: Taking someone else’s movable property for gain, without the owner’s consent, is theft (hurto). Below €400 it’s usually punished with a fine, but repeat offenders with at least three earlier theft convictions get the prison penalty. Disabling alarms or security devices increases the penalty.
answers.penalties: Over €400: 6 to 18 months in prison. €400 or less: a fine of 1 to 3 months’ daily rates.

answers.headline: Yes, but only truly hands-free: without holding the phone and without earphones.
answers.summary: Using a mobile phone or other communication system while driving is banned, unless the communication happens without using your hands and without headphones or earphones. Screens with internet access or video are also banned while the vehicle moves.
conditions: No hands
No headphones or earphones
answers.penalties: Using a phone in your hand: a traffic fine and points off your licence.

answers.penalties: A fine and points taken off your licence.

answers.headline: No. Assault is a crime in the Netherlands, with up to 3 years in prison, more if someone is badly hurt.
answers.summary: Assault (mishandeling) includes deliberately harming someone’s health. The penalty goes up if the victim is seriously injured or dies. Reasonable force in genuine self-defence (noodweer) can be lawful.
answers.penalties: Up to 3 years in prison; up to 4 years if it causes serious injury; up to 6 years if it causes death. Or a fine of the 4th category (€27,500).

answers.headline: No. Even if you didn’t know for sure, buying something you should have suspected was stolen is a crime.

answers.penalties: Knowingly: up to 4 years in prison. Should have suspected: up to 1 year. Either can instead carry a fine of the 5th category (€110,000).

answers.headline: No. Murder is one of the most serious crimes in the Netherlands, punishable by life imprisonment.

answers.penalties: Murder: life imprisonment or up to 30 years. Manslaughter: up to 25 years. Either can instead carry a fine of the 5th category (€110,000).

answers.headline: Technically illegal, but possessing up to 5 grams for personal use isn’t prosecuted.
answers.summary: Possessing cannabis is banned under the Opium Act, but under the official toleration policy (gedoogbeleid) the public prosecutor doesn’t prosecute possession of up to 5 grams for personal use. Coffeeshops may sell up to 5 grams per person per day, only to adults, and in most places only to residents of the Netherlands. Growing and supplying cannabis are not tolerated.
conditions: Up to 5 grams, for personal use
Coffeeshops: adults only, max 5 grams per day, usually residents only
answers.penalties: Above 5 grams police can confiscate it and you can be prosecuted. Up to 30 grams: up to 1 month’s detention or a 2nd category fine (€5,500); more is punished more heavily.
answers.regional_variation: Some cities enforce the residents-only coffeeshop rule more strictly than others. Ten municipalities take part in a regulated-supply experiment.

answers.headline: Yes, if you take part in the call yourself. Secretly recording other people’s conversations is a crime.

conditions: You must be a participant in the call
answers.penalties: Recording a call you’re not part of: up to 2 years in prison or a fine of the 4th category (€27,500).
